pos-env-file-checks:
Must have:
- Command line tool that checks environment variable files for problems
- Detects duplicated keys
- Detects style problems such as spaces around the equals sign or lowercase key names
- Exits with a non-zero status when it finds problems, so CI can fail on it
Nice to have:
- Can fix the problems it finds automatically
- Ready-made pre-commit or GitHub Actions integration
pos-clean-build-artifacts:
Must have:
- Scans a directory tree and finds software projects in it
- Recognises several ecosystems (Node, Rust, Python, Java and others), not just one
- Removes only regenerable artifacts such as dependencies and build output, never source code
- Asks for confirmation before deleting anything
Nice to have:
- Shows how much space each project would free
- Has a graphical interface besides the command line
pos-gmail-filters-as-code:
Must have:
- Gmail filters are described in a declarative configuration file
- Shows a diff of the changes before they are applied
- Applies the filters to the Gmail account through its API, with no manual import step
- Reduces long filter queries so they stay under Gmail's size limit
Nice to have:
- Imports the filters already in the account into the configuration file
- Lets filters be composed from reusable pieces
pos-many-git-repos:
Must have:
- Command line tool that registers many local git repositories
- Shows the branch and modification state of all registered repositories side by side
- Runs a git command on any registered repository from any working directory
- Runs the same git command on all registered repositories in a batch
Nice to have:
- Lets repositories be grouped
- Runs arbitrary shell commands, not only git, on the repositories
pos-terminal-site-monitor:
Must have:
- Command line tool, not a hosted service or a server to deploy
- Reports uptime and response times for a URL in real time
- Monitors several URLs at once from the command line or a config file
- Tracks SSL certificate expiry
Nice to have:
- Sends alerts to Slack, Discord or a webhook
- Exports metrics to Prometheus
pos-domain-name-brainstorm:
Must have:
- Command line tool that checks whether domain names are available
- Generates variants by combining a keyword with prefixes, suffixes and several top-level domains
- Checks many domains concurrently and shows results as they arrive
- Can print only the available domains
Nice to have:
- Machine-readable output such as JSON or CSV
- Saved presets of top-level domains
pos-baby-care-log:
Must have:
- Self-hosted web application
- Records sleep, feedings and diaper changes for a baby
- Shows the recorded history so patterns in the baby's needs can be seen
- Usable from a phone browser
Nice to have:
- Several caregivers can share the same data
- Tummy time and other activity tracking
pos-bank-statement-to-csv:
Must have:
- Converts bank statement PDFs into CSV
- Runs locally in a terminal, with no upload to a cloud service
- Supports statements from several different banks
- Handles password-protected statements
Nice to have:
- OCR for scanned statements
- Usable as a library from Python code
pos-invoice-data-extraction:
Must have:
- Extracts structured data (such as date, amount and invoice number) from invoice PDFs
- Handles different invoice layouts through templates written by the user
- Usable both as a command line tool and as a library
- Works without a paid cloud service
Nice to have:
- OCR fallback for scanned invoices
- Output as JSON, CSV or XML
pos-csv-json-into-sqlite:
Must have:
- Command line tool for working with SQLite databases
- Loads CSV, TSV or JSON data into a table directly from a pipe or a file
- Runs SQL queries from the command line and returns results as JSON
- Also usable as a Python library
Nice to have:
- Sets up full-text search on a table
- Changes table schemas in ways plain ALTER TABLE does not allow
pos-calendar-contacts-sync:
Must have:
- Command line tool that synchronises calendars and address books
- Works between a remote server and a local folder of files
- Syncs changes in both directions
- Supports CalDAV and CardDAV servers
Nice to have:
- Can also sync between two servers
- Runs unattended from a scheduler
pos-gps-track-video:
Must have:
- Creates a video from one or more GPS track files
- Draws the route on a map background
- Works from the command line, not only through a GUI
- Reads GPX files
Nice to have:
- Different map tile sources
- Control over video length and speed
pos-ios-dependency-notices:
Must have:
- Command line tool, not an in-app screen library
- Collects the notices of all dependencies listed by CocoaPods or Carthage
- Generates the files to put in the app's Settings.bundle
- Lets dependencies that were added by hand be included through a configuration file
Nice to have:
- Installable with Homebrew or Mint
- Separate list and detail screens in the output
pos-organise-photos-by-metadata:
Must have:
- Command line tool that organises photos and videos into a folder structure
- Uses metadata embedded in the files (date, location) to decide where each file goes
- Imports from a source folder to a destination folder
- Names folders after the place where each file was taken, translated from its GPS coordinates
- Can preview what it would do without changing any file
Nice to have:
- Customisable folder structure
- Handles audio files too
pos-strip-image-metadata:
Must have:
- Removes embedded metadata from images
- Processes a folder of files in one batch
- Runs locally and sends nothing over the network
- Shows the metadata of a file before and after cleaning
- Desktop application usable on Linux, macOS and Windows
Nice to have:
- Cleans PDFs and media files too
- Keeps the image orientation
pos-sonic-playlists:
Must have:
- Self-hosted tool that analyses the audio of a personal music library
- Generates playlists from sound similarity, not from metadata
- Works with an existing self-hosted media server
- Can start from one song and find similar ones in the library
Nice to have:
- Clusters the library into groups automatically
- Runs with Docker Compose
pos-subtitle-download:
Must have:
- Command line tool that downloads subtitles for video files
- Picks the subtitles that best match each video
- Lets the user choose one or more languages
- Scans a folder of videos
Nice to have:
- Usable as a Python library
- Skips videos that already have subtitles
pos-pgp-key-manager:
Must have:
- Interactive interface that runs inside the terminal
- Lists the keys in an existing PGP keyring
- Exports and signs keys from the interface
- Imports and deletes keys
Nice to have:
- Falls back to the command line for advanced operations
- Selectable colour styles
pos-container-to-run-command:
Must have:
- Command line tool that reads an existing container
- Prints the full docker run command that would create a similar container
- Includes ports, volumes and environment variables in that command
- Can read the output of docker inspect from standard input
Nice to have:
- Pretty-prints the command over several lines
- Works from a container name or id
pos-notebook-comparison:
Must have:
- Compares two versions of a notebook cell by cell instead of as raw JSON
- Three-way merge of notebooks with conflict handling
- Works from the terminal
- Integrates with git
Nice to have:
- Rendered web view of the comparison
- Automatic resolution of simple conflicts
neg-lease-key-dates:
Must have:
- Self-hosted web application for a tenant, not a landlord
- Reads an uploaded lease PDF and extracts the notice, renewal and rent review dates
- Sends reminders ahead of each notice deadline
- Publishes the dates as a calendar feed
Nice to have:
- Lets the user correct extracted dates by hand
- Keeps a history of rent changes
neg-terminal-runbook:
Must have:
- Records a shell session and turns it into a step-by-step runbook in Markdown
- Replaces hostnames, addresses and secret-looking values with named placeholders automatically
- Keeps the output of each command next to the command, trimmed to the relevant lines
- Runs locally with no cloud service
Nice to have:
- Lets a teammate replay the runbook with their own placeholder values
- Flags commands that were typed and then undone
neg-practice-tempo-log:
Must have:
- Records the user practising an instrument through the microphone
- Detects the tempo actually played, not the metronome setting
- Stores one entry per piece and per session
- Charts the tempo progress of each piece over weeks
Nice to have:
- Warns when the player speeds up during a passage
- Exports the log as CSV
neg-choir-practice-tracker:
Must have:
- Self-hosted web application for an amateur choir
- Imports a score as MusicXML and generates one practice audio file per voice part, with that part louder than the others
- Each member has an account and is assigned a voice part
- Logs which pieces each member practised and for how long
- Shows the choir director, per piece, which members have not practised yet
Nice to have:
- Adjustable tempo for the practice audio
- Reminder emails before rehearsals
neg-seed-library-germination:
Must have:
- Self-hosted web application for a community seed library
- Reads a photo of a seed packet with OCR and records the variety and harvest year
- Records germination test results for each batch of seeds
- Emails the members who borrowed a variety when its germination rate falls below a set threshold
Nice to have:
- Suggests which varieties should be grown out again this season
- Prints labels for repackaged seeds
neg-notes-open-actions:
Must have:
- Command line tool that scans a folder of Markdown meeting notes
- Collects action items assigned to each person across all files
- Marks an action item as done when a later note says it was completed
- Prints a list of the items still open per person
Nice to have:
- Shows how long each item has been open
- Output as Markdown or JSON
